---
title: "Correlation and Covariance with Linear Regression"
author: "Anthony Morciglio"
date: "11/12/2025"
output: html_document
---

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# =============================================
# Correlation and Covariance Visualization
# =============================================

# Load necessary library
library(ggplot2)

# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# Generate a dataset with a linear relationship
x <- seq(1, 50, by = 1)
y <- 2.5 * x + rnorm(50, mean = 0, sd = 10)  # Add some noise

# Compute correlation and covariance
cov_xy <- cov(x, y)
cor_xy <- cor(x, y)

# Display results
cat("Covariance between x and y:", round(cov_xy, 2), "\n")
cat("Correlation between x and y:", round(cor_xy, 2), "\n")

# Create a data frame
data <- data.frame(x = x, y = y)

# Fit a linear model
model <- lm(y ~ x, data = data)

# Create the plot
ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue", size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "red", linetype = "solid") +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation and Covariance Illustrated with Linear Regression",
    subtitle = paste("Covariance =", round(cov_xy, 2),
                     "| Correlation =", round(cor_xy, 2)),
    x = "Variable X",
    y = "Variable Y"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```


---

### 🧩 **What the Output Shows**
- The **console output** displays the numerical values for covariance and correlation.  
- The **plot** visualizes how the data points align around the regression line.  
- The **slope of the red line** represents the **direction and magnitude** of the linear relationship, consistent with the **sign of the correlation**.
